findings.evidence: SubscriptionModal enables editing payment_method (WALLET / GOOGLE_PLAY / GALAXY_STORE), but the post-update sync on open PLANNED rows (supabase.from("expenses").update({ title, category, game_id, original_price, final_amount })) omits payment_method and point_platform.
findings.impact: Non-blocking: auto_confirm_due_expenses reads v_tpl.payment_method directly and switching to WALLET forces t.auto_confirm = false, so ledger and auto-confirm behavior remain exact; however, an already-generated PLANNED row can retain its previous payment_method display label or manual payment modal default until the next cycle.
findings.recommendation: Include payment_method: paymentMethod and point_platform: paymentMethod === "WALLET" ? null : paymentMethod when syncing open PLANNED rows on template edits.

findings.evidence: expenses.auto_confirmed_at has no status invariant CHECK, the existing "Update own planned expenses" RLS policy allows an authenticated owner to update columns on their own PLANNED rows, and enqueue_daily_notifications() section 5 filters on e.auto_confirmed_at IS NOT NULL without checking status.
findings.impact: No cross-user, balance, or point-ledger risk (wallets, ledger, and user_finances remain strictly RPC-only and UI badges check status === "CONFIRMED"), but a user calling PostgREST directly on their own PLANNED row could self-trigger an EXPENSE_AUTO_CONFIRMED summary count or clear auto_confirm_blocked on their own row.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add CHECK (auto_confirmed_at IS NULL OR status <> 'PLANNED') (or guard auto_confirmed_at / auto_confirm_blocked in a BEFORE UPDATE trigger for non-definer callers) during a follow-up cleanup migration.
